file_name: Nicklas et al. - 2020 - Development and Modification of a Mobile Health Program to Promote Postpartum Weight Loss in Women a.txt

barriers.description: The app was developed and tested only on the iPhone platform, limiting the pool of participants and biasing the recruited sample.
barriers.justification: This platform choice constrained recruitment and participant diversity, hindering the team's ability to manage user understanding and understand the full context of use for the target population.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We developed and tested the Fit After Baby app on an iPhone Operating System platform. This affected the demographics and economic status of the recruited participants, which may thereby affect generalizability.

barriers.description: Participants often did not contribute to the online focus group weekly and many were unable to attend scheduled in-person focus groups.
barriers.justification: Irregular and last-minute participant availability limited the researchers' ability to facilitate user involvement and to evaluate and iterate on the design with consistent user feedback.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Consistent with the demands of women during this very challenging postpartum period, all participants did not contribute to the online focus group every week. Although we attempted to conduct 2 in-person focus groups, we had several women who were unable to attend at the last minute and had to convert the 2 focus groups to 2-person group interviews.

barriers.description: Technical integration and device issues (app switching and unreliable Fitbit syncing) caused participant frustration and incomplete activity data.
barriers.justification: Unreliable syncing and the need to switch between external apps reduced the quality and completeness of tracked data, hindering designers' ability to evaluate designs, integrate feedback, and iterate effectively based on user behavior.
barriers.reference_excerpt: they complained that their steps were not always syncing qith the Fit AFter Baby app. The majority of participants stated that they would have preferred a wrist band Fitbit, so we transitioned to this for the final version of the program.

barriers.description: The companion website was rarely used and was reported as not easy to use on mobile phones.
barriers.justification: Low website usage and poor mobile usability prevented designers from using the website as a channel to deliver content, view participant data, and collect feedback, limiting the team's ability to address the holistic experience and evaluate alternative delivery modalities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, the website was rarely used, and most participants stated that the website was not useful or that they did not use the website because it was not easy to use on their mobile phones. We decided to remove the companion website for the final iteration of the program.
